answer: Shared randomness challenge: each identity must answer a fresh, system-wide random challenge using a secret it committed to at creation. Because the challenge is identical across agents, one operator controlling many identities must produce correlated answers, a dune of sameness that stands out to auditors. A single identity leaves a hollow signature when it cannot vary independently. The signal of duplication is that correlation. Cost: each duplicate needs an independent secret and separate upkeep, multiplying the attacker's per-identity burden until copying fails.
